name: Hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Christianson-Fourie type

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic nail dystrophy including thickened, brittle, and discolored nails
Partial to total alopecia affecting scalp and body hair
Normal or near-normal sweat gland function distinguishing from hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: nail dystrophy, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and alopecia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not always available

laboratory: Normal sweat chloride test differentiating from hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia
imaging: Dental radiographs showing hypodontia or abnormal tooth morphology
genetic: Mutations in GJB6 gene (connexin 30) associated with Christianson-Fourie type
other: Clinical observation of nail and skin abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Similar nail and skin findings but often with earlier onset and more severe palmoplantar keratoderma
Genetic mutation in GJB6 but different variants
More pronounced dental anomalies and facial dysmorphism

redFlags: Severe palmoplantar hyperkeratosis causing functional impairment
Progressive nail dystrophy with secondary infection
Early onset alopecia with associated ectodermal abnormalities
references: Christianson CA, Fourie FR. A new variant of hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia. Am J Med Genet. 1984.
Orphanet Report Series: Hidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Christianson-Fourie type. Orphanet 2023.
Wright JT, et al. Ectodermal Dysplasias: Clinical and Molecular Review. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
